To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we propose ROADMAP, a robust and decomposable version of average precision that is suitable for end-to-end deep neural network training; (ii) we propose an algorithm that computes ROADMAP in a single forward pass of the network; (iii) ROADMAP can be used for training of image retrieval systems with deep neural networks.

we propose a robust and decomposable metric that is suitable for training of deep neural network architectures for image retrieval, and that we show that this metric can be used to train a state-of-the-art deep neural network architecture, which outperforms the state-of-the-art by a large margin on two standard image retrieval datasets.
ROADMAP is an end-to-end differentiable and decomposable average-precision metric, that can be used in a training loop for deep image retrieval networks.
